UK.b: One-year Masters, a strong brand and several fully funded awards.
UK.work: Graduate route: 2 years if you apply on or before 31 Dec 2026, and 18 months if you apply on or after 1 Jan 2027. PhD graduates get 3 years.
UK.money: Student visa: £1,529 a month for London courses or £1,171 a month elsewhere, for up to 9 months, held for 28 days.
watch: Chevening and Commonwealth close in October

US.b: The biggest choice of programmes. Funding mostly comes through assistantships.
US.work: F-1 students can work through Optional Practical Training, with a 24-month extension for STEM degrees. The length of initial OPT was not verified.
US.money: Proof of funds for the first year is required. Amount depends on the university (not verified).

CA.b: Thesis-based programmes often include funding, with a route to work after study.
CA.work: A 3-year Post-Graduation Work Permit is possible for Masters programmes of at least 8 months. Most applicants must give language test results.
CA.money: You must show enough money for tuition, living costs and return travel. The amount was not verified.

DE.b: Low or no tuition at many public universities, with strong engineering.
DE.work: Graduates can usually stay to look for work after the degree. Not verified.
DE.money: A blocked account is normally required for the visa. Amount not verified.

NL.b: English-taught Masters, high quality and compact cities.
NL.work: Orientation year permit: 1 year, apply within 3 years of graduating. A foreign degree must come from a top 200 ranked institution, and the diploma must be evaluated by Nuffic. Fee €254.
watch: Top-200 rule for the orientation year

SE.b: Strong research universities and a well-known government scholarship.
SE.work: Student work is capped at 15 hours a week for permits granted on or after 11 June 2026. Post-study permit rules were not verified.
SE.money: Maintenance of at least SEK 10,656 a month if you apply in 2026.

CH.b: Top science and engineering, with low tuition and high living costs.

FR.b: Strong in engineering, economics and social science, with the Eiffel scholarship.

AU.b: Wide choice, two intakes a year and a government awards programme.
AU.work: Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485) exists. Details not verified.

SG.b: Asia's global hub for engineering, computing and business.
SG.work: No dedicated post-study pass was found. Graduates usually move to an Employment Pass, which has a minimum salary and a points system.

JP.b: Top research universities, with the MEXT scholarship for research students.
watch: Supervisor often needs to accept you first

KR.b: Strong science and technology, with the GKS scholarship.

CN.b: Large scholarship programmes and fast-growing research universities.

EU.b: Joint Masters taught in two or more European countries, with full scholarships.
EU.work: Depends on the countries you study in.
watch: Each programme has its own application
